newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil consumer consumption seen dipping -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazil consumer consumption seen dipping -- poll.

text.p: An increasing number of Brazilian consumers expect to cut back on purchases over the next three months, a poll published Thursday showed.

The poll, carried out by the Brazilian Institute of Public Opinion and Statistics (Ibope) for the private National Industry Confederation (CNI), showed that 25 percent of people questioned intended to buy less in coming months.
In the last Ibope survey published November, 23 percent expected to cut consumption.
"This is not a drastic reduction in intended consumption but it is a reduction," said Flavio Castelo Branco, deputy head of the CNI's economics department.
CNI President Senator Fernando Bezerra, told reporters the survey results "refuted the idea that the economy is super overheating".
"It is clearly not true," he said, adding he hoped the reduction in spending intentions would result in an increase in domestic savings.

Strong second half growth in 1996 and the country's widening trade gap, which exceeded $2.0 billion in the first two months of 1997 alone, have led to speculation the government may slam the brakes on consumption.
Most recent comments from officials and also from the CNI have stated there was insufficient information at this time to determine whether or not the economy was growing too fast.

The Ibope survey, carried out between March 6-10 and for which 2,000 people across Brazil were polled, showed 52 percent of interviewees intended to maintain current purchasing levels against 54 percent in November.
Twenty-two percent intended to increase consumption versus 21 percent in November.
The Ibope survey also pointed to a greater sense of indebtedness among Brazilians, with 23 percent considering themselves more in debt versus 21 percent in November.
"The great conclusion we can draw is that the economy isn't overheating," said Bezerra.
